required_changes: Fail-closed gap in realizations.prepare_unit (realizations.py:224-242): reading-level optional_spans are only checked when the host fragment has its own optional_spans. Suppose a wording overlay's readings carry optional_spans but the host fragment has none, or the home lacks preserve_intrinsic_optionals. The check is skipped and the readings pass into alternatives unchanged. build.unit_document (build.py diff, the j:option branch) then emits marked j:conditional scopes for them. Neither the explicit flag nor the shape check (printed == '('+text+')', keys {printed,text,condition}, consistent conditions) is enforced. Raise if any reading has optional_spans unless the fragment has intrinsic optional_spans and the home flag is true.

Old behaviour changed in build.optional_words: the existing fragment-level path (formerly an inline loop at build.py:685-697) found each span with a sequential partition. It now requires text.count(printed) == 1 over the remaining text, and also rejects a span with empty or missing text. Accepted source with two identical printed spans in one fragment, e.g. '(x) … (x)' with spans [(x),(x)], built before and now raises. The xml:id scheme is unchanged. Either keep the sequential semantics for fragment-level spans and apply the stricter rule only to the new printing-overlay path, or regenerate every accepted Marmorstein project and show a byte-identical diff apart from the intended reprint change.
test_gaps: No test for a printing overlay whose readings carry optional_spans while the host fragment has none, or the home flag is absent. This is the bypass above.
No test for duplicate identical printed optional spans in one fragment, the old-behaviour regression case.
The flag test only removes the flag. Nothing tests non-True values (False, 'true', 1) for preserve_intrinsic_optionals or instructions_in_context, though prepare_documents rejects them.

No mutation tests for: span conditions in a different order between readings; extra span keys; a span text containing parentheses; choices[0].optional_spans differing from the fragment's spans; choices[0].text differing from the printed text.

Nothing asserts that the generated context/caller document has no marked j:conditional and no optional annotations. The test only counts conditionals in the home and checks that the home has no tei:note.

Nothing compiles the original main-service context (printing/main) across the four wife_children × parents profiles to show its output is unchanged apart from the new /prayer milestone. Both the unit test and compile-parnassah-optional-proof.py compile only the reprint caller (reading B).
The external-caller path is untested: a canonical occurrence carrying 'instructions' in a unit without canonical_home should be rejected.

Intrinsic optional_spans in a home with no wording overlay (fragment path plus the '(' ')' insertion in canonical_printings._selected_prefix) is untested. The shape printed == '('+text+')' is not enforced there; the prefix comparison probably fails closed, but only with an unclear error.
The new opensiddur:person kohen feature is not used or tested anywhere in this diff. No validate_features run covers a document that declares it.
notes: Otherwise the fail-closed design holds up. Both flags must be literally True, are stripped from the home config, and are listed in the allowed keys. The fragment and segment allow-lists widen only under their own flag. Instructions are validated as literal {language,text} in prepare_documents, canonical_text and validate_occurrence_controls, then removed from the home only. The generated pointer drops optional_spans and keeps instructions, which pass the CANONICAL_OCCURRENCE_KEYS check.

Adding 'instructions' to OCCURRENCE_CONTROL_KEYS does not change existing review hashes in attesting_controls, because canonical occurrence segments could not carry instructions before. It does newly add instructions to the payload for generated contexts that use the flag, which is intended.

In validate_occurrences (realizations.py:375 and :380) the instructions gate is written twice, and the second copy is unreachable. It reads the occurrence unit's own canonical_home. That is right for the generated context and stricter than needed (still fail-closed) for external callers.
The xml:ids generated for the fragment path are unchanged (stem_optional_<seg>_<idx>_<n>). The option path adds _optional_option_<seg>_<idx>_<reading>_<n>, and the test confirms the ids are unique.

The _selected_prefix handling is sound: it tracks nesting, ignores unselected options because their subtree is skipped, and refuses a page boundary inside optional words. It hardcodes '(' and ')' as the delimiters, which is valid only where the shape check has run.
No markup is duplicated in the home: the overlay pops fragment optional_spans after copying them into the readings, so each optional is emitted once per j:option and not again at fragment level.
Adding corresp …/yehi_ratzon/prayer to the old host paragraph changes structure but leaves the words alone, and the root URN is reused. Run validate_names on the new 'prayer' component.
